Subject: Pilot credits request — Campus AI Lab (undergrad research course)

Hi Karthik,

I'm Sandra Chen, Associate Professor in the Computer Science department at University of Centralia. We're running a new undergraduate AI lab this winter quarter (60 students, team projects) and would like to pilot Redwood Inference for several assignments and a small research cluster. This is non-commercial research and teaching; the students will not be using private student data other than course exercises.

High-level request: would Redwood consider providing free credits or a trial extension to support a 3-month pilot (Dec–Feb) for the course? Estimated usage: ~40k tokens/month (prompt+generation) per course overall, with a small spike during project demo week. We also have a small faculty research group that may run a few experiments — total anticipated consumption ~120k tokens for the pilot.

I've attached a brief letter from the department and a one-page grant summary (campus_ai_lab_letter.pdf, grant_summary.pdf). If you need an institutional contact, our grants officer is grants-office@ucentral.edu.

Next steps — could you advise on the information you need and typical timelines for EDU credit approvals?

Thanks,

Sandra Chen
Associate Professor, Computer Science
University of Centralia

Hi Sandra — thanks for reaching out and for the attachments. This sounds like a great use case. A few quick questions to help us route this internally and speed approvals: 

1) Can you confirm the expected average monthly token consumption and the projected max burst during demo week? You mentioned ~40k/month — is that the steady-state figure?
2) Will you need multiple API keys for students, or will you route requests through a single course account?
3) Any data sensitivity concerns (e.g., PII or student records) we should be aware of?
4) Do you require a private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or is hosted API acceptable for this pilot?
5) Please confirm institution name and whether the university is a non-profit/educational institution (we typically ask for an institutional approval letter — you've attached one which helps).

If you can send the answers, I'll loop in our customer success and security leads and propose an EDU promo package. Typical approvals for promotional credits take ~3–7 business days once we have the institutional docs and contact.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Education & Research
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Karthik — thanks for the quick reply. Answers below and attaching the signed institutional approval PDF.

1) Steady-state: ~40k tokens/month. Max burst: we expect one week (project demo week) where usage may hit ~80k tokens.
2) We prefer to create a single course API key managed by the instructor; individual student keys are not required.
3) Data sensitivity: low. Students will work with synthetic datasets or publicly available corpora; no student PII will be uploaded.
4) Hosted API is fine for this pilot. If the pilot succeeds we would discuss longer-term dedicated or private options.
5) University of Centralia — 501(c)(3) educational institution. Attached: institutional_approval_signed.pdf. Our grants officer (Marta Ruiz) is copied here: grants-office@ucentral.edu.

Let me know if you need anything else.

Best,
Sandra
